# CourtLine Android 1.0.22: registration safeguards and update marker

An already configured app now distinguishes new-device enrollment from reconnection. Scanning an enrollment QR shows an explicit warning that replacement creates a new device record requiring fresh Control permission and PIN. Cancel and Secure Reconnect are the preservation route. Intentional replacement requires a separate explicit button; no automatic credential or permission copying occurs.

Every saved-address reopen, discovered-address reopen, and Secure Reconnect migration checks that the returned viewer credential is unchanged and that the device ID matches whenever known. Device identity is persisted with a credential digest for restart checks. Older installations without persisted ID still require the same viewer credential. A failed identity check does not replace local pairing.

An available update now marks the main Settings control, in addition to the existing Options indicator, with accessible update text. The existing update checker and user-approved installation flow are unchanged.

Secure reconnection still requires Backend Test51+ and one trusted Secure Reconnect scan for legacy installations. Repeated normal network changes should not require further scans. Certificate renewal requires an explicit changed-certificate trust confirmation. Active-Control roaming is not automated; restart into Companion for startup discovery.

Validation: native build, original signer, executable Java identity and TLS guards, synthetic Android discovery, Backend51 TLS integration and updater runtime checks. Physical Fire tablet network discovery and visual rendering remain pending. This update cannot recover a previous credential already replaced by an earlier enrollment; administrators must explicitly identify and authorize the current device record.
